title: A World Without Mobile Phones!
body: Have you ever wondered how a message travels from your house all the way to a friend in another city? Today we just send a mobile message, but how did people communicate before phones existed? In ancient India, kings used trained pigeons (Kabootar) or messengers on horseback (Sandeshwahak) to send important messages across the country!

content.title: Imagine and Think
content.instruction: If you had to send a secret message to your friend who lives far away, and you had no internet and no phone, how would you send it? What are some ways you can think of?

content.title: The Journey of a Letter
content.description: Follow the letter as it travels from the red postbox, to the post office, onto a train, and finally to your friend's house!

title: What is a Letter?
body: A letter (Patra in Sanskrit and Hindi) is a written message addressed to a person. We write the message on paper, put it in an envelope, write the receiver's address, paste a stamp, and drop it in a Postbox.

content.description: A place where letters and parcels are collected, sorted, and sent to their destinations.
Postal Index Number. It is a 6-digit number that helps the post office know exactly which area the letter should go to.

content.tip: Explain that 'PIN' stands for Postal Index Number and show the students the local PIN code of your school's area.

content.question: Where do we drop our letters so that they can be sent to our friends?

content.mistake: Thinking that letters reach the very next minute like a mobile message.
content.correction: Letters take days to travel because they physically move via vans, trains, or aeroplanes.

content.title: If You Were a Postman...
content.instruction: Imagine you are a postman for a day. You have a big bag full of letters. What would be the most difficult part of your job? Discuss it with your classmates.

title: Connecting the Dots: Transport and Letters
body: Letters don't just magically fly! They need transport. Letters travel by trains, buses, and aeroplanes. So, sending a letter is connected to how good our transport system is.

content.title: Write Your Own Letter
content.instruction: Now it is your turn! Take a piece of paper, write a short letter to your friend, make an envelope, and draw a colourful stamp on it. Don't forget to write their address and PIN code!
